sources.title: GLM-5.3-Flash: How to Run Locally - unsloth.ai
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3-Flash can now run locally in Unsloth Desktop! GLM-5.3-Flash was trained on 30T tokens and is built on a newly trained base model redesigned. Its hybrid sparse and linear attention architecture lowers long-context serving costs without sacrificing accuracy, while Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections improve scaling.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 - Overview - Z.AI DEVELOPER DOCUMENT
sources.snippet: Overview GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's latest flagship model, delivering comprehensive advancements in complex software engineering and agent capabilities. It uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all improvements driven by post-training.

sources.snippet: Z.ai's launch blog is explicit about the strategy: test anonymously on OpenCode and OpenRouter, become "the most popular model of the week," then ship under the GLM brand with open weights. sources.title: Z.ai Releases GLM-5.3-Flash: A 320B-A18B Natively Multimodal MoE With a ...
sources.snippet: Z.ai has released GLM-5.3-Flash, the first natively multimodal model in the GLM-5 series and the cheapest capable coding model the lab has shipped. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 320B total parameters and 18B active per token, a 1,048,576-token context window, and image and video input — released under an MIT license with weights on Hugging Face.
